responsibilities: Own data domains end to end — from source system and ingestion, through dbt models in BigQuery, to the marts our analysts and BI tools build on
Design and build pipelines in Dagster+, orchestrating both dbt models and Python assets, with partitions, sensors, and automation conditions that fit the data rather than a cron guess
Model our data warehouse using dimensional modeling, and take a leading role in remodeling domains that have outgrown their original design
Set and hold the quality bar — data quality and freshness checks, meaningful tests, and monitoring and alerting so we find problems before our stakeholders do

Build and operate our data agents for modeling, monitoring, and analytics — design the workflows, tools, and guardrails, decide where an agent acts autonomously and where a human approves, and measure whether the output is actually good
Make the warehouse agent ready — treat metadata, documentation, data contracts and the semantic layer as production interfaces, because they are what agents (and people) reason from
Build data products and automations that put data to work directly in the business, not only in dashboards
Modernize and consolidate the platform — we are actively migrating legacy workloads onto Dagster and dbt, and paying down modeling debt as we go
Own your infrastructure as code with Terraform/Terragrunt, and treat DataOps (CI/CD, environments, branch deployments) as part of the job
Ensure compliance with data governance — high quality, secure, well documented and correctly retained datasets, including data deletion and privacy requirements
Work directly with stakeholders in Sales, Product, Finance and Engineering: turn a vague business question into a well-specified data model, and say no to the ones that should not be built

Raise the level of the team — thorough rubber ducking, code reviews, strengthening our conventions, writing the documentation that makes the platform learnable, and mentoring colleagues and new joiners

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Set and hold the quality bar — data quality and freshness checks, meaningful tests, and monitoring and alerting so we find problems before our stakeholders do
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Conventions, tests, data contracts and governance run throughout ("Set and hold the quality bar"), and there are no speed or shipping phrases.
evidence.domain_risk: the models you build are the ones the whole company reports on
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: An edtech platform whose models feed company-wide reporting affects business decisions; the single governance and privacy bullet does not make it a regulatory-reporting role, so it is moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: The Kahoot! Data Team is a small, cross-functional group of seven covering both data engineering and analytics.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A seven-person team with BigQuery, Dagster+ and dbt in the responsibilities and legacy workloads to migrate is an established but still growing function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design and build pipelines in Dagster+, orchestrating both dbt models and Python assets, with partitions, sensors, and automation conditions that fit the data rather than a cron guess
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name tools with exact application context ("partitions, sensors, and automation conditions"), so a reader knows the day-to-day work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: to the marts our analysts and BI tools build on
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is the analysts, BI tools and agents that consume the warehouse, with business teams served through them.
evidence.autonomy_level: Own data domains end to end
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns domains, sets the quality bar and decides "where an agent acts autonomously and where a human approves".
evidence.ai_role: Make the warehouse agent ready — treat metadata, documentation, data contracts and the semantic layer as production interfaces, because they are what agents (and people) reason from
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds the data agents and the agent-ready warehouse they run on, as well as using AI coding agents daily, so it is ai_enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Set and hold the quality bar — data quality and freshness checks, meaningful tests, and monitoring and alerting
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Tests, checks and alerting are an explicit responsibility the candidate owns.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: monitoring and alerting so we find problems before our stakeholders do
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Catching bad data before stakeholders see it is named, but the JD is dominated by building the agent-driven warehouse, so the risk register is secondary.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Modernize and consolidate the platform — we are actively migrating legacy workloads onto Dagster and dbt, and paying down modeling debt as we go
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Building new data agents ("We are building an agent-driven data warehouse") runs alongside migrating legacy workloads and remodeling domains.
evidence.loss_aversion: Set and hold the quality bar — data quality and freshness checks, meaningful tests, and monitoring and alerting so we find problems before our stakeholders do — reliability matters but is secondary to the agent build.
